linkedin.text:
More than ten years on Portland metro roofs has taught us a simple truth: fall is the season that decides everything. Whatever condition a roof is in when Oregon's rains start is the condition it fights winter in, which makes September and October the most valuable weeks on the whole maintenance calendar.

The late-summer pivot looks like this. Finish the dry-weather work first: trim branches overhanging the roof (the single best moss prevention there is) and close out lingering repairs. Then prep for the wet: clear valleys and gutters after the leaf-and-needle drop, recheck them after the first real storm, and apply moss treatment before the wet season gives spores their opening. Small fixes matter most now, because a loose shingle in October is a leak in December.

This carousel walks the full season-by-season rhythm we hand homeowners in Damascus, Clackamas, and Happy Valley. For owners who'd rather not track it themselves, our maintenance program covers it with spring and fall visits, inspection included.
